fichas.title: Hospital corridors
fichas.summary: Corridor dimensions should suit expected traffic. Bed-transport routes require wider usable clearances; service runs may be accommodated above a lowered suspended ceiling, subject to fire-protection requirements. Avoid internal corridors requiring mechanical smoke extraction, keep the usable width clear, and provide lighting and ventilation openings at appropriate intervals.

uses: Circulation for patients, staff, beds, deliveries, and services

fichas.title: Hospital doors
fichas.summary: Hospital door construction and finishes should meet sound-reduction, fire-protection, cleaning, and disinfection requirements. Clear opening dimensions vary by door type and function. T90 doors in firewalls should be held open so they do not obstruct traffic.

fichas.title: Hospital stairs
fichas.summary: Stairs should accommodate vertical traffic in an emergency and limit sound, odor transfer, and draughts. Provide handrails on both sides without free ends. Spiral stairs are not permitted as emergency stairs; stair doors must open in the escape direction and must not reduce landing clearance.

fichas.title: Hospital lifts and bed lifts
fichas.summary: Lifts transport patients, staff, supplies, and waste. Separate lift uses for hygienic and aesthetic reasons. Bed-lift cars should accommodate a bed and two accompanying people; interior surfaces should be washable and disinfectable, floors non-slip, and shafts fire-resistant. Provide a multi-purpose bed lift for every 100 beds, with additional smaller lifts for equipment and staff. The bed-lift table lists capacity, shaft, car, and door dimensions for three permissible loads.
